decision.coordinator_constraint: Accept only shared snapshot field projection with explicit copy/alias policy preserving each caller. Direct get_snapshot substitution changes ownership and is not behavior preserving. Independent reviewer identified this before coordinator feedback.

evidence.supports: Inline snapshot projection before response construction.
Normal accumulation replaces TokenUsage rather than mutating it; the counterexample concerns direct mutation of the retained object, not every subsequent completion.
Existing projection additionally deep-copies token usage.
TokenUsage is a mutable model with token fields.
Snapshot excludes detailed lists while Metrics owns accumulated data.

decision.label: duplicate
decision.proposed_extraction_or_counterexample: Boundary: replace only llm.py:460-465 with self.metrics.get_snapshot(), leaving transport, telemetry and response construction unchanged. This intentionally adopts the helper's deep-copy ownership rule and is not exact alias-preserving substitution. If strict current behavior is required, make token-usage copying an explicit keyword policy on the snapshot helper and pass false from completion. Counterexample: after returning a response, mutating metrics.accumulated_token_usage.prompt_tokens can affect the inline snapshot, but not the deep-copied snapshot. Keep this behavioral change explicit; do not claim the bodies are equivalent.
decision.reason: completion reimplements the MetricsSnapshot field projection already owned by Metrics.get_snapshot. The existing helper also isolates mutable token usage; the inline projection passes that object through. This is useful consolidation of a snapshot contract, with an explicit aliasing difference.
